messages:
jordan: Heads-up: noticed odd behavior in /v1/embeddings when a batch mixes an empty string, a normal short text, and a very long item — ordering seems preserved but truncation/resulting vector looks weird. anyone seen this?

priya: saw something like this in integration tests last week. do we truncate per-item or is there a batch-level token budget?

sam: per the current spec we intended per-item truncation to the model max context, but there was ambiguity for mixed input types (empty string / bytes). @jordan can you paste a minimal repro?

jordan: here's a quick curl i used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","inputs":["","short note","lorem ipsum repeated... (very long) "]}'
```

response: 200 with "data": [ {"embedding": [..1536 floats..] }, {"embedding": [..1536 floats..] }, {"embedding": [0,0,0,...] } ]

ordering preserved (good) but long item gave all-zero vector.

elaine: all-zero vector is interesting — historically we returned an error if an item exceeded hard token cap, but iirc we rolled a back-compat change to produce a placeholder vector for some failures to avoid breaking clients. might be hitting that path.

kevin: we changed behavior during the last inference runtime update: by default we now do a "best-effort" embedding for each item. if tokenization produces >per_item_hard_limit we either truncate (and return embedding) or on catastrophic tokenization failure return zeros. there is also an undocumented internal flag `strict_truncate` that flips it to error.

priya: is there a public parameter to control this? our SDK tests expect an error on oversized inputs. we need a stable opt-in to strict behavior.

sam: good call. for text generation we have `truncate: true|false`. embeddings currently have nothing. proposal: add `truncate_mode: "soft"|"strict"|"none"` where: soft = truncate per-item and return embedding; strict = return 400 if any item exceeds hard cap; none = try best-effort and may return placeholder (legacy). default should be "soft" for backward compatibility.

jordan: default to "soft" sounds safe. also can we document exactly what "truncate" means: per-item token cap vs batch token budget? our tests show two guards: max_items (1024) and total_batch_tokens (1_000_000). enforcement order matters.

elaine: yes, current runtime enforces: 1) reject if items > max_items; 2) compute token counts; 3) if total_tokens > batch_tokens_limit we reject the request; 4) per-item tokens > per_item_hard_limit => behavior depends on truncate_mode. i'll add this sequence to the API docs.

kevin: also we should guarantee returned shape is always [N, D] (N == input count). zeros should only be used for irrecoverable failure and be accompanied by a `warning` entry per-item in the response with machine-friendly codes (e.g., "TRUNCATED", "TOKEN_OVERRUN", "EMPTY_INPUT").

priya: adding structured warnings will make SDK handling easier. we can map warnings -> exceptions in strict mode. for now we'll patch the JS SDK to treat zeros+warning as a retriable/throwable state. filing EMB-432 for that.

jordan: one more question: empty string input — should we return a deterministic embedding (e.g., embedding of ""), or an explicit null/zeros? our integration tests expect a consistent vector (not null).

sam: i'd push to return deterministic embedding for empty string (tokenizer yields zero tokens but embedding of empty input should be stable). zeros reserved for failures, not legitimate empty inputs.

elaine: agreed. i'll update runtime so empty string -> canonical empty embedding. zeros-only reserved for failure codes, plus include `warnings` and `error_code` per-item as kevin suggested.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: embedding-runtime v2.7 -> prod at 03:00 UTC (reacted :rocket:)

jordan: :thumbsup: thanks. can we do a quick sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to align API wording + SDK changes? i'll drop a calendar invite.

kevin: i'll be there, will prepare a small diff for the OpenAPI schema and the migration notes.

priya: i'll update the JS SDK PR to accept `warnings` and the new `truncate_mode` param.

sam: i'll add unit tests for ordering + empty-string determinism.

elaine: i'll open the docs PR and a runtime follow-up issue to emit per-item warning codes.

jordan: awesome — thanks all.
